Standards for using Lenses.io developer tools and features to debug, monitor, and troubleshoot event-driven applications. These standards complement platform-level Lenses.io standards (see [Infrastructure Standards](../infrastructure/README.md#lensesio-kafka-management-platform-standards)).

Lenses.io provides powerful developer tools for inspecting Kafka topics, monitoring consumer lag, executing SQL queries, and visualizing data flows. **Platform**: [Lenses.io Portal](https://lenses.dev.company.com) (dev), [Production Portal](https://lenses.prod.company.com)

[standards/application/README.md#key-developer-features]

### Key Developer Features

**Topic Browser** ([STD-APP-KMGMT-001](kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-001-topic-browser-access.md)):
- Live message streaming (real-time tail)
- Historical message search (time range, offset, partition)
- Message filtering (key, value, headers)
- Format deserialization (Avro, JSON, Protobuf, String)
- PHI/PII data masking (automatic per STD-INFRA-KMGMT-010)
- Export to JSON/CSV (max 1,000 messages)

**LSQL Query Interface** ([STD-APP-KMGMT-002](kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-002-lsql-query-standards.md)):
- SQL-like syntax for Kafka topics (`SELECT * FROM topic WHERE field = 'value'`)
- Aggregations, joins, time windows
- Resource limits (30-second timeout, 10K rows max)
- Query history and saved queries
- Share queries with team

**Developer Dashboards** ([STD-APP-KMGMT-003](kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-003-developer-dashboards.md)):
- Custom dashboards per business unit/application
- Widgets: Topic throughput, consumer lag, error rates
- Real-time metrics (2-second refresh)
- Share dashboards with team

**Consumer Lag Investigation** ([STD-APP-KMGMT-008](kafka-management/STD-APP-KMGMT-008-consumer-lag-investigation.md)):
- Identify slow consumers and processing bottlenecks
- Partition-level lag breakdown
- Consumer group rebalancing history
- Lag trend analysis (predict SLA violations)
page_texts.28:
[standards/application/README.md#access-control--security]

### Access Control & Security

**Role-Based Access** (per [STD-INFRA-KMGMT-003](../infrastructure/kafka-management/STD-INFRA-KMGMT-003-rbac-access-control.md)):
- **Developer Role**: Access topics matching `{business-unit}.*` only
- **Production Developer Role**: Read-only production access with data masking
- **Read-Only Role**: View-only access to dashboards (no topic browsing)

**Data Masking** (per [STD-INFRA-KMGMT-010](../infrastructure/kafka-management/STD-INFRA-KMGMT-010-data-masking.md)):
- PHI/PII fields automatically masked (SSN: `XXX-XX-1234`)
- Visual indicator (🔒 icon) for masked fields
- Unmasked access requires approval (Manager + Data Steward + CISO)

**Rate Limiting**:
- Max 10,000 messages fetched per minute per user
- LSQL query timeout: 30 seconds
- Topic browser: Max 100 concurrent sessions
page_texts.29:
[standards/application/README.md#common-developer-workflows]

### Common Developer Workflows

**Workflow 1: Verify Message Publishing After Deployment**
1. Login to [Lenses.io Dev Portal](https://lenses.dev.company.com)
2. Navigate to topic: `{business-unit}.{application}.{event-type}`
3. Click "Browse" → "Live" mode
4. Verify new messages appearing with correct schema
5. Check message headers (correlation-id, timestamp, source)

**Workflow 2: Debug Consumer Lag Issue**
1. Navigate to "Consumer Groups" → Select your group
2. View partition-level lag breakdown
3. Identify stuck partitions (high lag, no progress)
4. Check consumer logs in CloudWatch (linked from Lenses.io)
5. Follow runbook: [Consumer Lag Troubleshooting](https://confluence.company.com/eaas/runbooks/consumer-lag)

**Workflow 3: Investigate Production Incident**
1. Request Production Developer access (if not already granted)
2. Browse production topic with time range (incident window)
3. Note: Data is masked (PHI/PII protected)
4. Apply filters: `$.status == "ERROR"` (JSON path)
5. Export error messages to JSON for offline analysis
6. If unmasked data needed, submit ServiceNow request with incident ticket

**Workflow 4: Execute Ad-Hoc Data Analysis**
1. Navigate to "LSQL" tab
2. Write query: `SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM claims GROUP BY status`
3. Execute query (max 30-second timeout)
4. Export results to CSV (max 10K rows)
5. Save query for future use
page_texts.30:
[standards/application/README.md#performance-guidelines]

### Performance Guidelines

**Topic Browsing**:
- Fetch max 100 messages at a time (pagination)
- Use filters to reduce result set
- Historical search: Limit time range (1h instead of 7d)

**LSQL Queries**:
- Use `LIMIT` clause to reduce result set
- Avoid unbounded time windows (use `WITHIN` clause)
- Test queries in dev before running in production

**Rate Limiting**:
- Respect 10,000 messages/min limit
- Stagger large exports (don't export 50 topics simultaneously)
- Use API for automation instead of UI scraping

### Relationship to Core Kafka Management

Integration monitoring standards **extend** core Kafka management standards:

- **STD-APP-INT-005** builds on **STD-APP-KMGMT-001** (Topic Browser) for cross-system tracking

page_texts.40:
[standards/application/README.md#common-integration-workflows]

### Common Integration Workflows

**Workflow 1: Trace Integration Flow End-to-End**
1. Select integration flow (e.g., "Claims Submission")
2. View topology: External System → API Gateway → Claims Service → Payment Service
3. Check message rates at each hop
4. Identify slowdown: Claims Service processing delays
5. Drill into Claims Service consumer lag

**Workflow 2: Validate Integration Transformation**
1. Use LSQL to query transformed messages
2. Compare source and target message formats
3. Verify data quality rules (completeness, validity)
4. Export sample messages for offline analysis

**Workflow 3: Monitor Third-Party Integration Health**
1. View integration dashboard for partner system
2. Check success/failure rates
3. Review anomaly alerts for unusual patterns
4. Escalate to partner if issues detected
